formation.title: The Electorate Ascendant
formation.text:
The Electorate of Saxony stands formed: second in the Empire only to the Emperor himself. The Wettin dynasty commands the richest mines in Christendom, the greatest trade fairs in Germany, and the constitutional power to shape the future of the Holy Roman Empire.

But what shall define Saxony's legacy? The Electorate gave birth to the Reformation, where Martin Luther's theses set the world ablaze. Wittenberg and Leipzig are centers of learning where new ideas flourish. Yet Saxony is equally renowned for its material splendor: the silver mountains, the porcelain works, the baroque magnificence of Augustus the Strong's Dresden.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the land of ideas and reformation

modifiers.name: Wittenberg Legacy
modifiers.text: From the steps of the Castle Church, a revolution of ideas swept across Christendom. Saxony's universities and printing presses shall be the instruments of a new age of learning, tolerance, and reform.

options.text: We are the Florence on the Elbe

modifiers.name: Augustan Splendor
modifiers.text: The silver of the Erzgebirge, the porcelain of Meissen, the palaces of Dresden: Saxony's wealth and magnificence shall make it the envy of every court in Europe.

advances.name: Erzgebirge Silver
advances.text: The Ore Mountains yield their treasures: silver discovered near Freiberg in 1168 launched a mining rush that would fund Saxon power for centuries.

advances.name: Freiberger Bergrecht
advances.text: The Freiberg Mining Code of 1296 established the rights of the 'free miner' and created one of Europe's earliest systematic legal frameworks for resource extraction.

advances.name: Trade Crossroads
advances.text: At the intersection of the Via Regia and Via Imperii, Leipzig's markets have drawn merchants since 1165, trading cloth, wine, spices, and metalwork.

advances.name: Wettin Retainers
advances.text: The mining communities of the Erzgebirge provide the Wettin court with sturdy militia, men hardened by the mountain tunnels who fight with the endurance of the stone they cut.

advances.name: Leipzig Messe
advances.text: Imperial privileges guarantee the Leipzig trade fairs safe conduct for all merchants, even those whose rulers are at war with Saxony.

advances.name: Cranach Werkstatt
advances.text: Lucas Cranach the Elder's workshop in Wittenberg produced paintings, woodcuts, and printed materials that shaped the visual language of the Reformation.

advances.name: Guldengroschen
advances.text: The first German Guldengroschen, issued from Saxony in 1500, established the precedent for large silver coinage that would evolve into the Thaler, and eventually the Dollar.

advances.name: Wittenberg University
advances.text: Founded in 1502 by Frederick the Wise, the University of Wittenberg attracted Martin Luther, Philipp Melanchthon, and a generation of reformers who would reshape Christendom.

advances.name: Schmalkaldic League
advances.text: The defensive alliance of Protestant princes, led by Saxony and Hesse, stood as the military shield of the Reformation against Emperor Charles V.

event.title: The Schmalkaldic League
event.text:
In February 1531, the Protestant princes of Germany gathered at Schmalkalden in Thuringia. Under the leadership of the Elector of Saxony and the Landgrave of Hesse, they forged a defensive alliance against Emperor Charles V, pledging 10,000 infantry and 2,000 cavalry for mutual protection.

The Schmalkaldic League represents the first organized Protestant military force in Europe. As the League's senior member, Saxony must decide how to wield this power.

options.text: Rally the Protestant armies under our banner

modifiers.name: Schmalkaldic Arms
modifiers.text: Saxon soldiers march alongside their Protestant brethren, committed to defending the reformed faith by force of arms.

options.text: Use our electoral prestige for diplomatic defense

modifiers.name: Schmalkaldic Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The Elector of Saxony wields constitutional prestige and diplomatic influence to forge a Protestant consensus, securing the reformed faith through negotiation rather than battle.

advances.name: Leipzig Book Fair
advances.text: Leipzig's annual book fair became the center of the German publishing industry, where printers, booksellers, and scholars gathered to trade in knowledge itself.

advances.name: Electoral Vicariate
advances.text: As Imperial Vicar, the Elector of Saxony governs in the Emperor's absence: a constitutional privilege that places Saxony at the heart of Imperial politics.

advances.name: Schneeberg Silver Rush
advances.text:
Rich silver deposits discovered at Schneeberg in 1470 sparked a second mining boom across the Erzgebirge, funding new towns and deeper shafts.

Available in: Silberbergwerk

advances.name: Furstenbund
advances.text: The League of Protestant Princes bound the reformed states of the Empire into a diplomatic bloc, with Saxony's electoral voice lending constitutional weight to the Protestant cause.

advances.name: Festung Konigstein
advances.text: The fortress of Konigstein, perched atop a sandstone mesa above the Elbe, has served as the Electorate's most impregnable stronghold since the medieval period.

advances.name: Albertine Administration
advances.text: The Albertine Wettins consolidated control over the Electorate through systematic administrative reform, creating a centralized bureaucracy that enhanced both revenue collection and state efficiency.

advances.name: Gewandhaus Tradition
advances.text:
The Gewandhaus (originally the cloth merchants' hall of Leipzig) became a symbol of Saxon commercial culture where trade in textiles built fortunes and civic institutions.

Available in: Messehaus

advances.name: Augustan Golden Age
advances.text: Under Augustus the Strong, Dresden was transformed into the 'Florence on the Elbe' with the Zwinger Palace, the Frauenkirche, and court cultural institutions that rivaled Versailles.

event.title: Florence on the Elbe
event.text:
Augustus the Strong dreams of transforming Dresden into a city to rival Versailles. The Zwinger Palace rises in baroque splendor, designed by Poppelmann and adorned with Permoser's sculptures. The Green Vault houses one of Europe's most dazzling treasure collections. Court painter Bernardo Bellotto captures the city's skyline in luminous detail.

The Frauenkirche's stone dome crowns the skyline. The Royal Opera cultivates a musical tradition that draws composers from across Europe. Dresden's golden age has begun.

options.text: Let the world marvel at Saxon magnificence

modifiers.name: Golden Dresden
modifiers.text: Under the patronage of Augustus the Strong, Dresden has become the 'Florence on the Elbe': a city of baroque palaces, world-class collections, and cultural magnificence rivaling any court in Europe.

advances.name: Porcelain Invention
advances.text: In 1710, Johann Friedrich Bottger perfected the production of European hard-paste porcelain in Meissen, breaking China's centuries-old monopoly on 'white gold.'

advances.name: Kursachsische Garde
advances.text: The Electoral Saxon Guard represents the professional standing army that replaced feudal levies, disciplined infantry in the latest European fashion.

advances.name: Grunes Gewolbe
advances.text: The Green Vault of Dresden houses one of the most dazzling treasure collections in Europe: a display of wealth and craftsmanship that enhances Saxon diplomatic prestige.

advances.name: Bergakademie Freiberg
advances.text: Founded in 1765, the Bergakademie Freiberg was the world's first university of mining sciences, training engineers who carried Saxon mining expertise across the globe.

event.title: The Bergakademie
event.text:
On 21 November 1765, Prince Francis Xavier of Saxony establishes the Bergakademie Freiberg: the world's first university of mining and metallurgical sciences. Born from the urgent need to revive the Erzgebirge mines after the devastation of the Seven Years' War, the academy quickly becomes a beacon of practical scientific education.

Abraham Gottlob Werner brings order to the world of minerals. Alexander von Humboldt studies here before his legendary expeditions. Scientists at the academy will go on to discover the chemical elements indium and germanium. The Bergakademie's model is copied from St. Petersburg to Mexico City.

options.text: Science shall renew what nature provided

modifiers.name: Bergakademie Science
modifiers.text: The world's first mining university has launched a revolution in applied science, training engineers and geologists whose methods transform industry across the continent.

advances.name: Constitutional Reforms
advances.text: The Saxon Constitution of 1831 established representative government, transforming the Electorate from absolutist rule toward a modern constitutional state.

advances.name: Publishing Capital
advances.text:
Leipzig's Borsenverein der Deutschen Buchhandler, founded in 1825, formalized the city's role as the publishing capital of the German-speaking world.

Available in: Druckhaus

advances.name: Saxon Industrialization
advances.text: Saxon textile mills and machinery workshops led Germany's industrial revolution, building on centuries of mining expertise and commercial tradition.

destiny.name: Saxon Destiny
destiny.text: Saxony stands formed: Electorate and great power. The path ahead is ours to choose: the life of the mind or the splendor of the court.

event.title: The Electoral Destiny
event.text:
The Electorate of Saxony is formed, and with it comes a question that will define our nation for centuries. The silver mountains fund our ambitions, the trade fairs draw merchants from across the continent, and the constitutional authority of the electoral vote gives us a voice that resonates throughout the Empire.

Now we must decide what kind of Saxony we shall build.

destiny.name: Cradle of the Reformation
destiny.text: Secure Wittenberg, the city where Luther's theses changed the world, and found a Library there worthy of a nation of learning, as Frederick the Wise gathered one for the Leucorea where Luther taught.

conditions.text: We own Wittenberg and it has a Library

event.title: Luther's City is Ours
event.text:
Wittenberg, where Martin Luther nailed his Ninety-Five Theses to the door of the Castle Church, now flies the Saxon banner. The university that educated Melanchthon and a generation of reformers is ours to nurture. The printing presses that spread Luther's words across Christendom are ours to direct.

This is more than a city. It is the birthplace of a revolution in human thought, and Saxony shall be its guardian.

options.text: The Reformation begins and ends in Saxony

destiny.name: The Printing Revolution
destiny.text: Saxon presses have reshaped the intellectual landscape of Europe. Hold Leipzig, whose book fair came to outsell Frankfurt's, raise it to 38 development, and let it grow from a town into a city.

conditions.text: We own Leipzig and it has grown into a city
We own Leipzig and its development is at least 38

event.title: The Power of the Press
event.text:
Saxon printing houses now dominate the German book trade. From Leipzig's fair halls to Wittenberg's university presses, the written word flows outward in an unstoppable current. Pamphlets, treatises, and scholarly works carry Saxon ideas to every corner of Europe.

But the press is a tool that can be wielded in different ways. Shall we use it to advance our diplomatic position, building networks of information and influence? Or shall we focus on building academic institutions that draw scholars from across the continent?

options.text: Deploy the press as an instrument of state

modifiers.name: Reformation Press
modifiers.text: Saxon printing houses serve as instruments of state policy, spreading ideas that undermine rivals and build diplomatic leverage through the power of information.

options.text: Build a network of academies and scholars

modifiers.name: Academic Network
modifiers.text: A web of Saxon-funded academies and scholarly exchanges draws intellectuals from across Europe, building soft power through the prestige of learning.

destiny.name: Enlightened Saxony
destiny.text: From Wittenberg to Strasbourg, Saxon ideas and Saxon institutions illuminate the continent. Found the Bergakademie at Freiberg, the first school of mining in the world, and establish Saxony as Europe's intellectual capital.

conditions.text: We own Freiberg and it has the Bergakademie

event.title: The Saxon Enlightenment
event.text:
From the Bergakademie in Freiberg to the university at Wittenberg, from Strasbourg's presses to Leipzig's book fairs, Saxon institutions have become the beating heart of European intellectual life. The Scientific Revolution has transformed how humanity understands the natural world, and Saxon scholars stand at its forefront.

This is the culmination of centuries of investment in ideas. How shall Saxony employ its intellectual supremacy?

options.text: Apply science to the art of governance

modifiers.name: Scientific Statecraft
modifiers.text: Enlightenment principles applied to governance produce a rationalized state apparatus, efficient, systematic, and ruthlessly effective.

options.text: Foster a republic of letters across borders

modifiers.name: Republic of Letters
modifiers.text: Saxon scholars correspond with intellectuals across every border, building a transnational network of knowledge that transcends the petty squabbles of dynasties.

destiny.name: The Bohemian Claim
destiny.text: The Wettin dynasty eyes the Bohemian crown. Take Prague and demonstrate that Saxon arms are as formidable as Saxon silver.

event.title: The Crown of Bohemia
event.text:
Prague, the golden city on the Vltava, has fallen to Saxon arms. The Bohemian crown (coveted by Habsburgs, Luxembourgs, and Jagellions alike) now adorns a Wettin brow. With Bohemia's wealth and manpower added to Saxon silver, we command resources that few in the Empire can match.

The road to German hegemony runs through conquered capitals. Prague is only the beginning.

options.text: Bohemia bends to the Wettin will

destiny.name: Northern Hegemony
destiny.text: From the Hanseatic ports of Lubeck to the Hohenzollern seat of Berlin, Saxon dominion must stretch across northern Germany.

event.title: Dominion Over the North
event.text:
The Hanseatic jewel of Lubeck and the Hohenzollern stronghold of Berlin both answer to Saxon authority. From the Baltic coast to the heart of Brandenburg, northern Germany has been brought under our control. Trade routes that once enriched our rivals now fill Saxon coffers.

How shall we consolidate this vast new dominion?

options.text: March our armies through the conquered cities

modifiers.name: Hanseatic Conquest
modifiers.text: Saxon armies have seized the great Hanseatic trade cities, and mercenary captains flock to serve a patron who pays in Erzgebirge silver.

modifiers.name: Saxon Dominion
modifiers.text: From Prague to Berlin, Saxon authority is enforced by disciplined garrisons and swift-striking assault forces that crush resistance before it can organize.

destiny.name: European Splendor
destiny.text: With Nuremberg secured and the treasury overflowing, Saxony can build a court to rival Versailles: a true Florence on the Elbe. Dresden must be held and raised to 44 development, and a Porzellanmanufaktur must be making the white gold that Meissen first made for Augustus the Strong.

conditions.text: We own Dresden and its development is at least 44

event.title: The Florence on the Elbe
event.text:
The dream of Augustus the Strong is realized. Dresden's baroque palaces rival Versailles, Meissen porcelain graces the tables of every European court, and the Green Vault's treasures dazzle foreign ambassadors. With Nuremberg's wealth secured and Saxon dominion stretching across Germany, we have built something that will endure for centuries.

Shall our legacy be remembered for its cultural magnificence or for the military power that made it possible?

options.text: Let the world marvel at our magnificence

modifiers.name: Baroque Magnificence
modifiers.text: The baroque splendor of Saxon palaces, collections, and court life makes Dresden the cultural capital of the German-speaking world, though such magnificence does not come cheap.

options.text: Forge a Saxon empire in iron and silver

modifiers.name: Saxon Imperium
modifiers.text: A military-economic empire built on cavalry, mercenaries, and the vast revenues of conquered German territories.

units.name: Erzgebirge Bergleute
units.text: Mining militia from the Ore Mountains, hardened by their work underground and fighting with the endurance of men who dig through stone.

units.name: Kursachsische Garde
units.text: The Electoral Saxon Guard, disciplined professional infantry of the standing army, trained in the latest tactical doctrines.

buildings.name: Silberbergwerk
buildings.text: A Saxon silver mine in the Erzgebirge, extracting the precious ore that has funded the Wettin dynasty since the 12th century.

where.text: Silver is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Messehaus
buildings.text: A Leipzig trade fair hall where merchants from across Europe gather under imperial safe conduct guarantees to exchange goods and forge commercial ties.

buildings.name: Cranach Werkstatt
buildings.text: An artistic workshop in the tradition of Lucas Cranach the Elder, producing fine prints, woodcuts, and illuminated materials that spread Saxon culture.

buildings.name: Druckhaus
buildings.text: A Saxon printing house producing books, pamphlets, and scholarly works, the engines of the Reformation and the German Enlightenment.

buildings.name: Hofkapelle
buildings.text: The court chapel and music ensemble of Dresden, a cultural institution that drew composers and musicians from across Europe to perform under Saxon patronage.

buildings.name: Porzellanmanufaktur
buildings.text: A porcelain factory producing Meissen-style hard-paste porcelain, Europe's answer to Chinese 'white gold,' bearing the famous crossed swords mark.

buildings.name: Bergakademie
buildings.text: A mining academy following the Freiberg model, training engineers and metallurgists in the scientific methods that transformed the mining industry.

buildings.name: Aufklarungsschule
buildings.text: A Saxon Enlightenment academy dedicated to the advancement of natural philosophy, applied science, and rational governance, the institutional embodiment of the Saxon intellectual tradition.

buildings.name: Dresdner Schloss
buildings.text: The grand palace of the Saxon Electors, rebuilt in baroque magnificence to house the Green Vault, the royal art collections, and the most dazzling court in Germany.

list.name: Bergordnung
list.text: The Schreckenberger Bergordnung of 1499/1500 (the oldest printed mining code in Europe) and Duke George the Bearded's expanded Annaberg ordinance of 1509 codified the rights of free miners (Bergfreiheit), fixed shifts and ore-shares, and protected miners from feudal lordship. The code became the model for mining law across Central Europe and underwrote the great silver rush in the Erzgebirge at Schneeberg, Annaberg, and Marienberg.

list.name: Oberbergamt zu Freiberg
list.text: Founded on 1 July 1542 by Duke Maurice and headquartered at Freiberg, the Saxon Mining Office was the oldest formal mining authority in Germany. The Oberbergamt placed the entire Bergstaat (Bergmeister, smelting works, foundries, and miners' wages) under direct electoral control. Its multi-tiered bureaucracy channeled the Erzgebirge silver flow into the Wettin treasury and made Saxony the wealthiest of the German principalities.

list.name: Sachsisches Konsistorium
list.text: Established at Wittenberg in 1539 under Elector Johann Friedrich, the Saxon Lutheran Consistory took over marital jurisdiction, ecclesiastical discipline, and parish visitations after the abolition of episcopal offices. With the elector serving as summus episcopus, the Consistory's jurists and Wittenberg theologians standardized Lutheran doctrine, ran the Latin Schools, and made Saxony the institutional heartland of the Reformation.

list.name: Geheimes Konsilium
list.text: Formalized under Elector Christian I in the 1580s and elaborated under Augustus the Strong around 1706, the Privy Council was a small body of trusted ministers that worked in secret on finance, war, and foreign policy. By bypassing the Landtag entirely, the Konsilium became the institutional spine of Saxon absolutism and managed the dual Saxon-Polish union from the Dresdner Schloss.

list.name: Sachsische Landstande
list.text: First convened by Elector Frederick II in 1438 and meeting regularly thereafter, the Saxon Landtag gathered prelates, counts, knights, and the deputies of the Saxon cities to negotiate tax grants and, increasingly, fiscal, military, and religious policy. Unlike most German Landtage the Saxon estates were unusually resilient: they bargained with the elector rather than being dictated to, and survived as a real check on princely power well into the 18th century.

list.name: Leipziger Reichsmesse
list.text: King Maximilian I confirmed Leipzig's three annual fairs in 1497 and in 1507 elevated them to Reichsmessen (imperial trade fairs) with empire-wide safe-conduct for merchants and a Bannmeile of fifteen miles within which no competing fair could be held. The privileges drew merchants from Venice, Cracow, Frankfurt, and Hamburg and made the burgher capital, not Dresden, the engine of the Saxon economy.
